name: web/particles-3d
title: 3D particles
summary: One HTML file with a moving 3D field of particles: stars, snow, rain, fireflies, a turning galaxy or confetti. It can be turned and zoomed with the mouse or a finger.
when: Use when the user wants a moving field of particles in 3D: a starfield, falling snow or rain, fireflies, a galaxy, confetti, or a particle animation they can turn with the mouse.

title.about: A short name for the page, shown in the browser tab and at the top left.

kind.about: What the particles do, in plain words: stars, snow, rain, fireflies, galaxy or confetti. A whole sentence works; the page takes the first of these words it finds.

color.about: The color of the particles: a CSS color name or a hex code. The word own keeps each kind's own color.

count.about: How many particles, a number from 100 to 6000. The word own keeps the kind's own count.

next: Nothing more to do: the page is finished and shows itself in the chat. Do not read it, run it, build it or install anything; tell the user in one or two sentences what the page shows. Only when the user asks for a change: edit the settings lines inside <script type="text/plain" id="settings"> in index.html with replace_in_file.
change: Make one call per change: replace_in_file(path="{file}", old="kind stars", new="kind snow") changes the kind (stars, snow, rain, fireflies, galaxy, confetti); the color and count lines work the same way, for example old="count 2000", new="count 3500". Only the three lines inside <script type="text/plain" id="settings"> near the top of index.html are edited; nothing else changes.

not_text: Kind not understood, showing stars. Known kinds: stars, snow, rain, fireflies, galaxy, confetti.
Color not understood, using the kind's own color.
